long_biography.plain_text:
Ken Griffin's interest in computers preceded his career in finance: as a teenager, he sold software to educational institutions. At Harvard, he began trading convertible bonds, installed a satellite dish on his dormitory roof for real-time market data and launched a small hedge fund using quantitative analysis. After graduation, he moved to Chicago to work with Frank Meyer, whose backing helped him establish the fund that became Citadel.

Griffin developed Citadel around the combination of specialist talent, advanced analytics and powerful software. He and his partners later founded Citadel Securities as options trading moved towards electronic markets, creating a separate market-making firm. His civic work now runs through Griffin Catalyst, an initiative supporting education, science and medicine, community resilience, upward mobility and enterprise.
